section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the Upward Physical Appearance Comparisons Subscale (O'Brien et al., 2009), a 10-item measurement instrument rated on a 5-point scale that assesses the tendency to make upward appearance-based social comparisons. The scale has demonstrated reliability and validity in prior research with Australian undergraduate men. The authors note they used only the upward comparison subscale to reduce participant burden, as upward comparisons are theoretically and empirically more potent for body image outcomes than downward comparisons.
